newsitem.title: USA: US stocks down but off lows at midday.
newsitem.headline: US stocks down but off lows at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks climbed off their lows on slim volume at midday but remained in negative territory after a spate of surprisingly strong economic numbers undermined bonds and raised fears of Fed tightening.
The Dow Industrials were down 37 points at 5611 after sinking as low as 5588 earlier and triggering the NYSE's automatic curbs on some program trades at 1004 EDT/1404 GMT.
"One would think the market is factoring in a 25 basis point increase in the Fed funds rate next month," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

The most important new economic data today was the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index, a precursor to next week's National Association of Purchasing Management report. The Chicago Index jumped to a surprising 60.0 in August from July's 51.2.
"That is the report that more than any other was responsible for the sell-off in stocks and bonds," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"It hints that manufacturing activity was strong throughout the country, and that will be reflected in next Tuesday's NAPM and Friday's employment numbers."
He added, "What the Chicago PMI tells you is to get ready for some unfriendly numbers next week."
Adding insult to injury, the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for August rose to 95.3 from July's final reading of 94.7.

Among July economic figures reported today, factory orders rose 1.8 percent, compared to a 0.7 percent increase in June, personal income rose 0.1 percent, compared June's 0.9 percent increase, and personal consumption rose 0.2 percent, compared to June's 0.4 percent drop.
Low trading volume and the fact that the economic data surprised Wall Street pros exaggerated the stock market's move, said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

"A lot of participants are not active, so you get exaggerated moves," he said. "The most significant factor is that all this is a surprise. The consensus had been for a significant slowdown in the economy which would forestall an increase in interest rates."
The Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24.
"This was supposed to be a good day," Johnson said. "The last three days before Labor Day have been strong for the last 17 years." The market will be closed Monday for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.

Among special situations, Boatmen's Bancshares rose 10-12/16 to 53-11/16 and topped the Nasdaq most active list on news of its planned merger with NationsBank Corp . NationsBank was down 7-1/4 at 85-1/8 in active trading.
Dell Computer was up one at 67-5/9 on news that it would replace Varity Corp in the S&P 500 Index after the close of trading on September 5.
